items.text: • MXL does not define a control API, so documenting requirements will help promote interoperability.

items.title: How does it work?
items.text:
• Gives requirements for setting paramters and querying status of MXL Writers and Readers.

This work artifact is published as an AMWA Increment (IN). Increments are intended to make public the ongoing progress of a working group without locking decisions into a formal specification. While the technical details contained in this repository do not constitute a stable or finalized specification, readers should note that Increments are Draft Specifications as defined in the AMWA IPR Policy. The provisions of the policy apply, including the requirement for early disclosure. You can expect the content to evolve incrementally based on ongoing testing, consensus-building, and community input. Public review is encouraged! Please post an Issue to the Repo to submit questions, feedback, or propose changes.

items.title: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 1. Purpose
items.text:
This document defines the functional and non-functional requirements for a control API that manages MXLReaders and MXLWriters in a DMF environment.

The API enables a control system to:

  • Set parameters in MXLReaders and MXLWriters.
  • Query their current status.

This document is intended for implementers of control protocols that provide this API.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 2. Scope
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 2.1 In Scope
items.text:
• Control of MXL Readers
  • Control of MXL Writers
  • Querying current parameter values:
  • MXLDomainID
  • MXLFlowID
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 2.2 Out of Scope
items.text:
• Mapping of Domain ID to Flow Path
  • This mapping must be configured when deploying the media function and is not handled by this API.
  • Media transport, encoding, or payload-level processing
  • Control of processing parameters
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 3. Definitions
items.text: Term Description MXLReader Component that consumes media from an MXLFlow. MXLWriter Component that produces media into an MXLFlow. MXLFlowID UUID of a media flow as defined in the MXL SDK. MXLDomainID UUID of the domain in the same format as the MXLFlowID.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 4. Architecture Assumptions
items.text:
• MXLReaders and MXLWriters are part of Media Functions deployed by an orchestration system.
  • Deployment is outside the scope of this document.
  • MXLDomains and MXLDomainIDs are created outside the scope of this document.
  • Media Functions can resolve MXLDomainIDs to MXLDomains (paths) and vice versa.
  • An MXLReader or MXLWriter can have access to one or more domains.
  • An MXLReader or MXLWriter has a mechanism for discovering the MXLDomains mapped into its filesystem.
  • If a writer is started without a configured FlowID, it will create one.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5. Functional Requirements
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.1 MXLReader Requirements
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.1.1 Set and Get MXLFlowID
items.text: • The API shall allow setting, updating, and retrieving the MXLFlowID of an MXLReader.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.1.2 Set and Get MXLDomainID
items.text:
• The API shall allow setting, updating, and retrieving the MXLDomainID of an MXLReader.
  • Invalid or inaccessible MXLDomainIDs shall result in a validation error.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.1.3 Start MXLReader
items.text:
• The API shall provide a method to start the read operation of an MXLReader.
  • Starting an already running MXLReader shall be idempotent.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.1.4 Stop MXLReader
items.text:
• The API shall provide a method to stop the read operation of an MXLReader.
  • Stopping an already stopped MXLReader shall be idempotent.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.1.5 Get Accessible MXLDomains
items.text: • The API shall allow retrieving a list of all MXLDomainIDs from which the MXLReader can read flows.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.2 MXLWriter Requirements
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.2.1 Set and Get MXLFlowID
items.text: • The API shall allow setting, updating, and retrieving the MXLFlowID of an MXLWriter.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.2.2 Set and Get MXLDomainID
items.text: • The API shall allow setting, updating, and retrieving the MXLDomainID of an MXLWriter.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.2.3 Start MXLWriter
items.text:
• The API shall provide a method to start the write operation of an MXLWriter.
  • Starting an already running MXLWriter shall be idempotent.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.2.4 Stop MXLWriter
items.text:
• The API shall provide a method to stop the write operation of an MXLWriter.
  • Stopping an already stopped MXLWriter shall be idempotent.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 5.2.5 Get Accessible MXLDomains
items.text: • The API shall allow retrieving a list of all MXLDomainIDs to which the MXLWriter can write.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 6. API Behavior and Constraints
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 6.1 Creation of FlowID
items.text:
• The FlowID of a writer is not created by the control system.
  • It is created either by:
  • The orchestration system, or
  • The writer itself.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 6.2 State Management
items.text:
• Readers shall expose their current operational state:
  • started
  • stopped
  • Writers shall expose their current operational state:
  • started
  • stopped
  • Readers and writers shall expose their current transport parameters, including:
  • MXLFlowID
  • MXLDomainID
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 6.3 Error Handling
items.text:
All API errors shall return a structured error response containing:

  • Error code
  • Human-readable message
  • Optional remediation hint
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 6.4 Idempotency
items.text: • Start and stop operations shall be idempotent.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 7. Non-Functional Requirements
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 7.1 Reliability
items.text:
• The API shall guarantee consistent state reporting.
  • Partial updates shall not leave readers or writers in undefined states.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 7.2 Performance
items.text: • Control operations (start, stop, configure) should be responsive and complete in a timely manner.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 7.3 Security
items.text: • It is assumed that any API implementing these requirements will operate in an environment with security measures appropriate to the associated risks.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0

items.title: 7.4 Observability
items.text: • Operational monitoring requirements will be defined in a future revision of this document.
path: API Requirements – Control of the Media Exchange Layer (MXL) v1.0
